title: Domain-wall drift in a ferrimagnet induced by a linearly oscillating in-plane magnetic field
abstract: We investigate ferrimagnetic domain-wall dynamics under linearly oscillating in-plane magnetic fields. Starting from a ferrimagnetic Lagrangian that retains the field-dependent contribution to the kinetic energy, we derive collective-coordinate equations for the domain-wall position and azimuthal angle. This formulation makes explicit the field-induced inertial terms, including Coriolis-, Euler-, and centrifugal-like contributions, and clarifies how they couple translational and azimuthal dynamics. For an oscillating in-plane field supplemented by a weak static out-of-plane bias field, we show that periodic switching of the wall angle can be rectified into a finite average domain-wall velocity. At low drive frequencies, where the wall angle follows the oscillating field, the induced drift is proportional to the drive frequency rather than the field amplitude, while above a cutoff frequency the wall angle can no longer follow the drive and the average motion is suppressed. Micromagnetic simulations confirm the analytical predictions and demonstrate that the magnitude and direction of the drift can be tuned by the net spin density. These results identify linearly oscillating fields as a mechanism for frequency-controlled domain-wall motion in ferrimagnets and highlight the role of inertial spin dynamics near magnetic compensation.
summary: This work analyzes domain wall motion in ferrimagnets driven by oscillating magnetic fields. By deriving collective-coordinate equations that explicitly include inertial coupling terms, the authors predict a frequency-controlled rectification of the domain-wall drift velocity. This mechanism offers a novel way to control magnetization dynamics using time-varying fields.
main_problem: The study investigates how domain walls move within ferrimagnetic materials when subjected to a linearly oscillating in-plane magnetic field.
main_result: The system exhibits a rectified, finite average domain-wall velocity proportional to the drive frequency at low frequencies, which is suppressed above a critical cutoff frequency.
method: The authors derived collective-coordinate equations of motion from an effective Lagrangian, incorporating inertial terms like Coriolis and centrifugal forces, and confirmed results via micromagnetic simulations.
model_or_system: The model describes ferrimagnetic domain walls in two coupled sublattices ($\mathbf{M}_i$), whose dynamics are governed by LLG-like equations projected onto collective coordinates $\{X(t), \Phi(t)\}$.
key_observables: Average domain-wall velocity ($\langle\dot{X}angle$), wall angle ($\Phi$), and position ($X$).
important_parameters: Oscillation frequency ($\omega$), net spin density ($\delta s$), and the static out-of-plane bias field ($H_z$).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses a rigid collective-coordinate ansatz for the domain wall, and approximations are made regarding terms smaller than $M_s H / A_0$ away from compensation.
figures_summary: Figures confirm that the DW velocity shows a linear dependence on frequency below a cutoff and is suppressed above it; the drift velocity is shown to be proportional to the net spin density ($\delta s$).
paper_structure: The paper derives effective equations of motion by projecting the full LLG dynamics onto collective coordinates, analyzes the resulting inertial couplings (Coriolis, Euler), and then applies this framework to an oscillating field case to derive the frequency-dependent drift velocity.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the derivation of generalized inertial terms (Coriolis/centrifugal) from a Lagrangian formalism is highly relevant to understanding non-linear dynamics in quantum systems, such as those modeled by effective Hamiltonians for trapped ions or superconducting circuits.
